Consequently,

j^2 - (j - 1)^2 = j^2 - (j^2 - 2j + 1) = 2j - 1.

This is an exact algebraic identity. In fact, it holds in any commutative ring with identity, although only integer values are needed here.

THEOREM 2: Telescoping proof of the odd-integer sum formula.

Claim: For every integer n >= 0,

S_n := sum_{j=1}^n (2j - 1) = n^2.

Proof: First suppose n >= 1. Applying Theorem 1 term by term,

S_n = sum_{j=1}^n [j^2 - (j - 1)^2].

Writing out this finite sum explicitly,

S_n = (1^2 - 0^2) + (2^2 - 1^2) + (3^2 - 2^2) + ... + (n^2 - (n - 1)^2).

S_n = n^2 - 0^2 = n^2.

S_n = sum_{j=1}^n j^2 - sum_{j=1}^n (j - 1)^2
 = sum_{j=1}^n j^2 - sum_{k=0}^{n-1} k^2
 = n^2 - 0^2
 = n^2.

Boundary case n = 0: By the empty-sum convention,

S_0 = sum_{j=1}^0 (2j - 1) = 0 = 0^2.

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1) = b^2 - a^2.

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1)
= sum_{j=a+1}^b [j^2 - (j - 1)^2]
= [(a + 1)^2 - a^2] + [(a + 2)^2 - (a + 1)^2] + ... + [b^2 - (b - 1)^2].

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1) = b^2 - a^2.

An equivalent calculation uses Theorem 2:

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1)
= sum_{j=1}^b (2j - 1) - sum_{j=1}^a (2j - 1)
= b^2 - a^2.

Boundary case a = b: The lower index becomes b + 1, so the sum is empty. Hence

sum_{j=b+1}^b (2j - 1) = 0 = b^2 - b^2.

Thus the generalized identity holds whenever 0 <= a <= b.

sum_{j=1}^n (2j - 1) = n^2 - 0^2 = n^2.

sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (2j + 1) = n^2.

sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (2j + 1)
= sum_{k=1}^n (2k - 1)

S_n := sum_{j=1}^n (2j - 1) = n^2.

S_n = sum_{j=1}^n [j^2 - (j - 1)^2].

S_n = (1^2 - 0^2) + (2^2 - 1^2) + (3^2 - 2^2) + ... + (n^2 - (n - 1)^2).

 = n^2 - 0^2
 = n^2.

S_0 = sum_{j=1}^0 (2j - 1) = 0 = 0^2.

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1) = b^2 - a^2.

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1)
= sum_{j=a+1}^b [j^2 - (j - 1)^2]

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1) = b^2 - a^2.

sum_{j=a+1}^b (2j - 1)
= sum_{j=1}^b (2j - 1) - sum_{j=1}^a (2j - 1)
= b^2 - a^2.

sum_{j=b+1}^b (2j - 1) = 0 = b^2 - b^2.

Thus the generalized identity holds whenever 0 <= a <= b.

sum_{j=1}^n (2j - 1) = n^2 - 0^2 = n^2.

sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (2j + 1) = n^2.

sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (2j + 1)
= sum_{k=1}^n (2k - 1)
